decision_conditions: The proposal, by virtue of the constraints of the application site, would fail to ensure the safe egress and exit of vehicles in a forward gear onto Victoria Road, and would lead to a further proliferation of crossovers and an increase in the number of conflict points on this section of the highway. The proposal would thereby be detrimental to highway and pedestrian safety and result in the disruption of the free flow of traffic, and be contrary to the objectives of Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021), Policies DMT 1 and DMT 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2: Development Management Policies (2020), and the requirements of the Council's 'Domestic Vehicle Footway Crossover Policy' (2022).

The proposal, by reason of the loss of the majority of the soft landscaped front area and existing grass verge - for which no details of any replacement soft landscaping or mitigation has been provided - would be detrimental to the visual amenity and character of the area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy BE1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part One Strategic (2012) and Policies DMHB 11 and DMHB 12 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan - The Spatial Development Strategy for Greater London (2021) and national guidance.
